topic: Open Source and Other OS (Linux, Unix, Android)
description: An exam-oriented study guide covering the architecture, historical development, and core concepts of Open Source software, focusing specifically on Linux, Unix, and Android operating systems.

sections.title: Open Source vs Closed Source
sections.description: Classification of software based on its distribution model and source code availability.

key_concepts.explanation: Software whose source code is publicly available for free. Anyone can read, modify, and distribute it to suit their needs. Examples: Linux, Mozilla Firefox, VLC Media Player.
Software whose source code is kept secret and restricted. It can only be modified, legally copied, or distributed by its original creator or publisher. Examples: Microsoft Windows, macOS.
A non-profit organization founded by Richard Stallman in 1985 that promotes the universal freedom to study, distribute, create, and modify computer software.

important_facts.fact: The GNU Project was launched by Richard Stallman with the goal of creating a completely free operating system, which later became foundational to the development of Linux.

sections.title: Unix Operating System
sections.description: The history and key technical characteristics of the highly influential Unix OS.

key_concepts.explanation: Unix is designed to allow multiple users to work on the system simultaneously while executing multiple programs or tasks at the same time.
A crucial component of the Unix architecture that acts as a command-line interpreter or interface between the user and the core operating system (Kernel).

historical_events.significance: Unix was initially developed at AT&T Bell Labs by a team including Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie.

important_facts.fact: Unix was the first major operating system to be primarily written in the 'C' programming language, making it highly portable across different hardware platforms.

sections.title: Linux Operating System
sections.description: Core architecture of Linux and its most widely used distributions.

key_concepts.explanation: The core component of the Linux operating system. It manages hardware resources (CPU, memory) and facilitates communication between software applications and the hardware.
A complete operating system package built around the Linux kernel, bundled with various software, utilities, and a package management system.

historical_events.significance: Developed by Finnish computer science student Linus Torvalds and released freely under an open-source license.

key_associations.associated_with: Ubuntu, Fedora, Debian, Red Hat Enterprise Linux (RHEL), Kali Linux
key_associations.extra_info: Kali Linux is highly specialized and widely used worldwide by professionals for cybersecurity, digital forensics, and penetration testing.

important_facts.fact: The official mascot of the Linux operating system is a smiling, stylized penguin named 'Tux'.

sections.title: Major Linux/Unix Commands
sections.description: Fundamental commands used on the Command-Line Interface (CLI) in Linux and Unix environments.

key_associations.extra_info: Displays all the files and folders present in the current working directory.
Outputs the full absolute path of the directory the user is currently located in.
Used to create one or multiple new directories (folders) in the file system.
Used to navigate through the file system by moving from one directory to another.
Controls and modifies the read, write, and execute permissions of a file or directory for different users.
Used to permanently delete files or directories from the system.

sections.title: Android Operating System
sections.description: The world's most popular open-source operating system designed for touchscreen mobile devices.

key_concepts.explanation: Android is fundamentally an open-source mobile operating system that is built upon a modified version of the Linux kernel.
The standard file format used by the Android operating system for the distribution and installation of mobile applications.

historical_events.event: Release of the First Android Device
historical_events.significance: The HTC Dream (also known as T-Mobile G1) became the first commercially released smartphone to run on the Android operating system.

important_facts.fact: Android was originally founded and developed by Android Inc., which was subsequently acquired by Google in 2005.
The Open Handset Alliance (OHA) is a commercial consortium of technology companies (including Google, HTC, Sony, and Samsung) that played a vital role in developing open standards for Android.
